text:
B is better. Its DST examples are correct: a 3-day gap across spring forward is 71h, which floors to 2. Its fix uses `Math.round`, so the result is a whole number and the `=== 0` and `=== 1` checks work. A's replacement code drops rounding entirely, so it returns fractional days and breaks those checks, even though A's prose suggests rounding. A also wrongly says the fall-back case can put an invoice in the wrong place on the overdue list, when the sign is still correct and only the label is affected. B states this correctly.

B
